newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines not heading for property collapse.
newsitem.headline: Philippines not heading for property collapse.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos said on Tuesday the local property sector was not about to crash.

"We feel there are enough safeguards in our laws to prevent a further decline or collapse (in the property sector) as feared by some analysts," Ramos told news conference in the central Sorsogon province.
Manila stocks, led by property issues, took a beating on Tuesday on persistent fears that the industry was about to follow the property bust in Thailand.
Bank issues have also been hit on fears they have extended large loans to real estate firms.
The main index tumbled 2.87 percent, or 84.53 points, to 2,860.45.
"The Philippines is different from Thailand," Ramos said.
"The Philippine property sector has been forewarned of not overdoing it. Our banking community likewise has been warned of overheating by no less than the governor of the Central Bank," he said.
"Our macro-economic fundamentals which we have put in place are very, very sound," Ramos added.
Besides Thailand, the Philippines has also been compared with Mexico and the Mexican peso crisis which rippled through the emerging countries from the end of 1994.

"We went though the more difficult Mexican crisis...and we survived that. We were able to clear up our own situation within two months even if there is a striking similarity between the Latin American (country) and the Philippines," Ramos said.
